title: Interest earns interest
learning_goal: Contrast simple and compound interest using a hypothetical two-year example
subject: finance

approved_facts.statement: In this hypothetical example the starting principal is $1,000, with no additional deposits or withdrawals.
At a hypothetical 10% annual rate compounded annually, year one adds $100 of interest, giving $1,100.
Year two interest is 10% of $1,100, or $110, giving $1,210. The extra $10 is interest earned on year one interest.
Simple interest at the same hypothetical 10% rate on the original $1,000 adds $100 each year, giving $1,200 after two years.
The 10% rate is an illustrative assumption, not a prediction or guaranteed investment return. Compound interest earns interest on prior interest.
